dataset_family: National Cheng Kung University Hospital (NCKUH) memory clinic, Tainan, Taiwan: retrospective MCI cohort seen January 2017 - December 2019, 86 MCI (40 converted to dementia within 3 years, 46 stable)
method_family: Brain perfusion SPECT (99mTc-ECD) quantified with the easy Z-score imaging system (eZIS severity, extent, ratio). Comparator: Scheltens visual medial temporal atrophy (MTA) rating on MRI, not volumetry. Analysis: stepwise binary logistic regression and ROC
what_it_shows: In a three-year MCI follow-up, eZIS perfusion indicators were higher in converters (all p<=0.025). Visual MTA also discriminated converters (MTA 3-4 in 21/40 converters vs 9/46 stable, p<0.01). eZIS severity predicted conversion with AUC 0.719, essentially equal to MTA (AUC 0.720); the AUCs were not formally compared. In a stepwise binary logistic regression that offered both MTA and the eZIS indicators, conversion was independently associated with MTA (OR 3.05), eZIS severity (OR 5.35) and baseline CDR-SB (OR 3.08). Perfusion therefore carried information beyond the visual atrophy rating, and matched it in discrimination. Hippocampal or whole-brain volume was never measured.
why:
Pai, Matsuda and Pai 2024, Diagnostics 14(16):1780, doi 10.3390/diagnostics14161780. The PDF title, authors and DOI match the summaries.md block and the map entry. The extract was read in full to the References: methods, results, Tables 2-7, Figure 2 caption, discussion and limitations.

DECODING NOTE: the captions of Tables 5 and 6 appear swapped. The table carrying odds ratios (p.7-8) is captioned 'cognitive function test score deterioration ... by multiple regression', but its column header is 'Conversion from MCI to Dementia'. The table carrying coefficients (p.8-9) is captioned 'conversion ... by binary logistic regression', but its columns are Delta CASI, MMSE and CDR-SB. The text (p.7) states that the binary logistic regression for conversion 'revealed a positive correlation between the conversion and MTA and eZIS severity and baseline CDR-SB'. I rely on the text plus the column headers. The OR values used here (MTA 3.05, severity 5.35, CDR-SB 3.08) are from the table whose column header is conversion.

STATED FORM (Table A1): no. Atrophy was not preserved. MTA scores differed strongly between converters and stable patients (p<0.01, Table 2, p.4), MTA was an independent predictor of conversion, and MTA's AUC (0.720) equalled that of the best perfusion indicator (p.7). The study therefore does not show perfusion predicting conversion where atrophy is preserved, and it does not show atrophy as late or insufficient. The comparator is also a visual rating, not volumetry.

NARROWED FORM (round 20): partly. Within the study, a non-volumetric measure (SPECT perfusion) (a) predicted MCI-to-dementia conversion at parity with an MRI atrophy measure (AUC 0.719 vs 0.720; the authors say 'the AUC for MTA closely approximated that for severity', p.10), and (b) was retained alongside MTA in a joint stepwise logistic model, i.e. carried information that the atrophy rating did not (p.7-8). That is the shape of the narrowed wording. MTA also remained discriminative, consistent with its last sentence. It is 'partly' because the narrowed wording is about VOLUME ('carried information that volume did not'; 'at least as well as hippocampal volume'). Here the comparator is a 0-4 visual rating of choroid fissure, temporal horn and hippocampal height (p.3), read by a single author. That is a coarse proxy for hippocampal atrophy, not a volumetric measurement. Further limits: stepwise selection; no AUC comparison test; a single-centre retrospective sample of 86; no amyloid or tau confirmation; eZIS normed on Japanese data (p.10). If the operator accepts visual MTA as standing in for hippocampal volume, the study meets the narrowed wording's parity and complementarity strands.

METHOD FAMILY: SPECT perfusion is closest to the statement's 'metabolic' (or 'functional') family. No current supporter uses SPECT perfusion.

INDEPENDENCE: new dataset (Tainan, Taiwan) with no overlap with the current supporters' samples, sites or authors, or with the other candidates (P-224 Qatar, P-44 Busan, P-183 ADNI). The corresponding author (Ming-Chyi Pai) also appears on another corpus paper (summaries.md line ~42786, Kung et al.), which is not a VF-20 supporter or candidate. Not a preprint. Not in registry_duplicates.json.

The block does not mention the MTA comparison or the joint regression; both come from the PDF. Quotes are rejoined across line breaks, with typographic characters normalised to ASCII.

quotes.quote: In addition, the Fazekas scale of deep white matter hyperintensity (DWMH) and periventricular white matter hyperintensity (PWMH) and Scheltens' medial temporal atrophy (MTA) were obtained [19,20].

The MTA score was graded from 0 (no atrophy) to 4 (severe atrophy) based on the width of choroid fissure, width of temporal horn, and height of hippocampal formation [20]. Both the Fazekas scale and MTA score were visually interpreted by author YTP.

In addition, binary logistic regression was performed to predict the conversion from MCI to dementia based on the variables mentioned in multiple regression, see Table 6. The result revealed a positive correlation between the conversion and MTA and eZIS severity and baseline CDR-SB.

The optimal cut-off values with the largest AUCs were 1.22 for severity (AUC = 0.719), 10.48 for extent (AUC = 0.712), and 1.01 for ratio (AUC = 0.698). To compare the predictive ability of MTA and eZIS indicators for the conversion from MCI to dementia, we conducted a further ROC analysis focusing on MTA. The optimal cut-off value, yielding the largest AUC, was found to be 2.5 for MTA (AUC = 0.720, sensitivity = 0.525, and specificity = 0.804), see Figure 2.

As shown in Figure 2, the AUC for MTA closely approximated that for severity. However, it is important to note that a limitation of MTA is its subjectivity, whereas the eZIS provides a relatively objective assessment.
Finally, the development of the eZIS used parameters based on Japanese norms, and the accuracy of the eZIS application to Taiwanese patients must be carefully interpreted.
